entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Vistula–Oder Offensive was a pivotal event in the latter stages of World War II, launched by the Soviet Red Army and Polish Army against Nazi Germany on January 12, 1945. This major military campaign took place in Poland and lasted until February 2, 1945, marking a significant turning point in the war on the Eastern Front.

The offensive was a culmination of the Soviet Union's push towards Germany, following the successful capture of Warsaw in January 1945. The Soviet and Polish forces, led by General Konstantin Rokossovsky and Marshal Georgy Zhukov, respectively, launched a massive assault on the German army, which was already weakened by the war.

The Vistula–Oder Offensive resulted in the capture of over 200,000 German soldiers, a significant loss for the German army. The campaign also led to the capture of several major cities in Poland, including Krakow and Warsaw, and paved the way for the eventual Soviet occupation of Eastern Germany.

The legacy of the Vistula–Oder Offensive can be seen in the subsequent expulsion of Germans from Poland, which led to the displacement of millions of people. The event also marked the beginning of the end of Nazi Germany's control over Eastern Europe.
